nodes.plm_action: Apply Mod Podge on top of cardboard
nodes.plm_caption:
This video shows a person giving an instructional video about making a decorative phone case. In the beginning of the video there is a woman who introduces the video. Behind her is a hot pink sign that says "CREATIVE CREATIONS" in black text. She uses a smartphone with a pink floral case to demonstrate how to cover a case.
The first step of making a case is to cover the back of the phone. She lays a white piece of cardboard on the back of the phone. The person then gets a wide red piece of cardboard and places it on top of the white one. She uses a small brush to spread Mod Podge on the back of the phone. Then she takes a strip of fabric and places it over the top of the red cardboard. She slides the fabric onto the back of the phone and uses the same brush to apply Mod Podge to the back of the fabric. She then places the pink floral phone cover onto the back of the phone and uses the same brush again to spread Mod Podge onto the cover, then places the phone inside. The woman introduces herself at the beginning and end of the video. At the end, there are a lot of photos of DIY phone cases. She also shows the logo for "Creative Creations."

summary.brief: A woman demonstrates how to turn a hardcover book into a magnetic phone case, holder, stand, and wallet.
summary.detailed: The video opens with the presenter standing in front of a pink "CREATIVE CREATIONS" sign and greeting viewers. She gathers a hardcover book, a phone case, a magnet, a metal paperclip, Mod Podge, a paintbrush, water‑based glue, scissors, an X‑Acto knife, a ruler, a pencil, a strip of fabric, a piece of plastic for a pocket, and Velcro. She cuts the pages of the book to match the size of her phone, then traces the phone case on the inside of the book and cuts an opening for the screen. A strip of fabric is glued to both sides of the magnet, the magnet‑fabric assembly is folded and glued to the front edge of the book, and a paperclip is glued as a magnetic latch. She coats the exterior of the book with Mod Podge, adds an additional decorative material layer, cuts holes for the latch, and creates a pocket from plastic that is glued inside the book and attached to the phone case. Velcro is applied to the back of the phone case and to the inside of the book, the phone is placed inside, and the completed hybrid case, holder, stand, and wallet is shown. The tutorial ends with the presenter thanking viewers and a series of promotional slides featuring other Creative Creations projects.

action.detailed: Cut the book to the phone's dimensions, glue a fabric‑covered magnet to the front and attach a paperclip latch, coat the exterior with Mod Podge, add a plastic pocket inside, affix Velcro to the case and book, and insert the phone to create a combined case, stand, holder, and wallet.

This video shows the process of making a DIY phone case. The person is applying decorative paper to the back of a phone case and using a small book as a base. They also use a phone and a small bag as a paper weight. The process takes about 15 seconds and includes several shots of the person explaining the process.
The woman begins by showing a phone case with a phone in it. She then flips the case open and reveals a book underneath. She then opens a small book and flips through its pages. She then takes a paint brush and dips it in some Mod Podge. She then puts that Mod Podge on the book and folds the pages of the book. She then takes the paper case of the phone and adds some floral print tape to its back. She then uses Mod Podge to keep the tape in place. She then presses the case onto the back of the book and applies pressure all around the edges. After that, she places a small piece of tape on the back of the phone and adds some more decorative tape and Mod Podge.

summary.brief: A presenter shows how to turn a hardcover book into a magnetic phone case that also works as a holder, stand, and wallet.
summary.detailed: The video opens with a title screen and the presenter introducing the DIY project. She lists the supplies: a hardcover book, cutting board, X‑Acto knife, ruler, pencil, scissors, Mod Podge, paintbrush, water‑based glue, a magnet, a metal paper‑clip, a phone case and Velcro. First she removes all of the book’s pages with the knife and sets them aside for other crafts. She then cuts a block from the cover that matches the dimensions of the phone, places the phone case inside the book, traces its outline with a pencil and cuts the shape out with the X‑Acto knife. On the opposite side she draws and cuts a decorative front opening. Next she prepares a strip of material, glues the non‑magnetic side, positions it beside a magnet, coats the magnet’s sides with Mod Podge, flips the material over and glues it around the magnet’s edges. She folds the piece, glues a paper‑clip to the front of the book, and attaches the magnet strip inside so the magnetic side faces outward. She coats the exterior of the book with a layer of Mod Podge, covers it with decorative material, presses it into the creases, then flips the book and adheres the same material to the interior, cutting openings for the two holes that will hold the phone. She cuts another piece to fit inside the book and glues it in place, trims excess around the holes, and creates a pocket from a thin plastic sheet by inserting cards, folding the bottom piece, trimming excess, and wrapping the sides around the back before gluing it to the inside of the phone case. Finally she applies Velcro to the back of the phone case and to the inside of the book, aligns them, secures them together, places the phone inside, and declares the multifunctional case/holder/stand/wallet complete.

action.detailed: Cut the book to the phone’s size, trace and cut the case shape, attach a magnet and paper‑clip with glue and Mod Podge, cover the exterior with Mod Podge and decorative material, create pocket openings, affix Velcro inside the book, then insert the phone into the finished assembly.
